## 2B.4 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Mostly yes, but with a thin direct record.** The strongest 2024 evidence shows Marcos’s government emphasizing **restraint, incident prevention, and non-offensive conduct** in South China Sea operations. I did **not** find credible evidence of prisoner mistreatment or civilian-targeting, and I found no clear report of disproportionate force. The main limitation is that the available record is mostly **maritime standoffs and coordination**, not full combat operations.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced a formal South China Sea **incident-prevention and management** agreement plus coast-guard cooperation. That is strong evidence of operational caution and proportionality-minded risk reduction. | `2B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.3` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PH, China agree to 'calmly deal' with incidents in S. China Sea](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217166) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-01-18 | The DFA said both sides would **calmly deal** with incidents, improve maritime communication mechanisms, and avoid escalation. This supports restraint and communication discipline in operations. | `2B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.3` |
| E3 | Favorable | [We’re ordered not to be provoked by China’s aggressive actions in WPS - PCG](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/were-ordered-not-to-be-provoked-by-chinas-aggressive-actions-in-wps-pcg/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-05-04 | A PCG official said personnel were under a chain of command and ordered **not to be provoked** while maintaining professionalism. This is direct evidence of command discipline and restraint under pressure. | `2B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.3` |
| E4 | Favorable | [PBBM salutes troops in dangerous Ayungin resupply mission](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-salutes-troops-in-dangerous-ayungin-resupply-mission/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-06-23 | Marcos praised Western Command troops for **“the greatest restraint”** during a violent resupply mission. This is the clearest evidence that he rewarded restrained conduct rather than retaliation or disproportionate escalation. | `2B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.3` |
| E5 | Favorable | [Marcos rejects use of water cannons to retaliate vs. Chinese vessels](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would **not** use water cannons and had no intention of attacking with offensive measures. That is direct evidence of necessity and proportionality-minded restraint. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.5` |
| E6 | Favorable / limiting context | [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-06-23 | Marcos said the Philippines was **not in the business of instigating wars** and would settle disputes peacefully, refusing force or intimidation. This supports a broader non-reckless operational posture, though it is not a detailed IHL statement. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.5` |
| E7 | Limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training. This shows a deterrence-heavy posture that could increase risk, but it is not evidence of civilian harm, prisoner abuse, or IHL violations. | `2B.4`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E8 | Limiting context | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) - Reuters, 2024-12-05 | Maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan continued after later confrontations. This indicates sustained operational tempo, but I found no reporting tying it to civilian harm or disproportionate force. | `2B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.8` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 2B.4:** Marcos repeatedly endorsed **restraint**, **incident prevention**, and **non-offensive conduct** in maritime operations.
- **Best limiting evidence:** The Philippines also pursued a **deterrence-heavy posture** with allied drills, but those reports do not show unlawful or disproportionate violence.
- **Search gap:** I found **no credible 2024 evidence** on prisoner treatment because there were **no reported prisoner/detainee cases** in the relevant incidents. I also found **no reliable reporting of civilian-targeting, unlawful strikes, or clear humanitarian-law violations** in Marcos-directed operations.

**Working judgment for 2B.4:** **Mostly yes.** The operational record points to **restraint and proportionality**, but the direct IHL evidence is limited because the year’s main security episodes were maritime confrontations rather than full armed engagements.
